## Description

Spontaneously immortalised human keratinocytes (the cells of the epidermis). Epithelial and
polygonal, 20–25 µm when rounded and ~40 µm spread. They grow in islets that merge until they cover the
dish and differentiate at confluence; used to study wound closure.

## In the simulation

<!-- GENERATED:presence -->
Drops: not seeded in the default drops (inoculate it from the Catalogue).
<!-- /GENERATED -->

An adherent [animal cell](../../mechanics/animal-cells.md) with a G1/S/G2/M cycle, crawling migration, contact
inhibition and glucose/glutamine metabolism from the data.

## Literature

- Boukamp P. et al. (1988) J. Cell Biol. 106: 761 (origin of the line).
- Cellosaurus CVCL_0038: doubling time 28 h.
- PLoS ONE (2012), doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0031711, table 2: isolated HaCaT 63 ± 15 µm/h (46 in
  groups, 32 confluent; assignment to be verified).
- Alberts B. et al. *Molecular Biology of the Cell*, 6th ed., fig. 17-4 (S 8 h, G2 4 h, M 1 h of a typical human cell).
- Carruthers A. (1990) Facilitated diffusion of glucose. Physiol. Rev. 70: 1135–1176 (GLUT1 Km ~1–3 mM).
- Cytion data sheet (size).

## Not implemented yet

- No cell–cell adhesion: cells do not form true islets.
- No differentiation at confluence.
- Persistence, confluence density and metabolism are estimates; not yet validated like the
  fibroblast and HeLa.
- No phase-contrast lens yet: cultures are seen in bright field (roadmap C).
- Not supported in the well-mixed culture.

## Unique and shared mechanics

Shares the [animal-cell machinery](../../mechanics/animal-cells.md) with the fibroblast, NIH/3T3 and HeLa.
